newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica fuel industry to decide Taiwan deal- paper.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica fuel industry to decide Taiwan deal- paper.

text.p: A group of South African petrochemical companies are poised to make a decision this week on whether to pursue a Taiwanese proposal for a 3.5 billion rand greenfields petrochemical complex to be built somewhere off the coast of South Africa, Business Day newspaper reported.
The paper quoted Trevor Munday, managing director of petrochemical company Polifin Ltd as saying a meeting between the various participants had been scheduled for "later this week".
Earlier this month the Taiwanese vice-premier Hsu Li-teh said South Africa had pledged full support for the petrochemical plant and was likely to submit its proposal by the end of September.

The companies considering the 50/50 venture between Taiwan and South Africa include Polifin, Engen Ltd, the Central Energy Fund and the Industrial Development Corp, Business Day said. Sentrachem Ltd, Sasol Ltd and AECI Ltd are also believed to be involved.
South Africa's trade and industry department was also promoting the proposal, the paper said.
Hsu said earlier this month that if the project went ahead Taiwanese experts calculated that a total of 80,000 jobs could be created.
